what: Hand-labelled precision sample for the duplication finder — the metric the product now depends on.
method: Top-N findings from two repositories, ranked as a user sees them, each judged by reading the code at both anchors. TRUE if a developer would want to be told before writing similar code; FALSE if the two regions merely share a shape (JSX scaffolding, hook declarations, unrelated object/Set literals, lists of string literals).
bias: Labelled by the tool's own author, on repositories the author knows. This is a floor-check, not an independent evaluation, and it should be redone by someone with no stake before the number is used in a pitch.

after.ranking: longest aligned run, clustered into findings
after.note: n is small because the alignment filter removed 26 of 34 seenit pairs outright. Those removals were overwhelmingly the JSX false positives, but a filter that discards most candidates needs its RECALL checked, which is not done.

seenit.note: The one survivor that is still wrong is a run of const [x, setX] = useState(null) shared between App.jsx and StructurePanel.jsx. Every other JSX false positive was removed by the alignment filter.

vite.note: Not re-labelled after the ranking change. Clustering collapsed a style.css copied across 22 create-vite templates from roughly 200 pairs into one finding, which was the largest readability problem at this scale.

trueExamples: lib/analyze/metrics/score.js grade() vs src/lib/api.js healthColor() — the same 90/80/70/55 threshold ladder encoded twice; changing a band means editing both
calibration/corpus.mjs vs calibration/history.mjs — mulberry32 PRNG copy-pasted verbatim
calibration/collect.mjs vs calibration/corpus.mjs — an identical four-line flag() argument parser
calibration/collect.mjs vs lib/analyze/index.js — collect.mjs reimplements fileRecord()
bin/seenit.mjs health() vs mcp/server.js review_changes() — both reimplement analyze-then-compare-to-previous
packages/create-vite/template-react vs template-preact vs template-solid — the same App component per framework
falseExamples: src/App.jsx vs src/components/StructurePanel.jsx — a run of const [x, setX] = useState(null)
src/App.jsx vs src/components/HealthPanel.jsx — a JSX return with className and style props
calibration/apply.mjs FALLBACK vs score.js WEIGHT_PROVENANCE — two unrelated object literals
lib/analyze/extract.js BRANCH vs lib/analyze/parser.js SKIP_DIRS — two unrelated new Set([...]) literals
vite docs socialLinks vs team.js links — two unrelated arrays of { icon, link } objects
knownGaps: RECALL IS UNMEASURED and is now the binding constraint. The relative cutoff trades recall for precision — it removed the last JSX false positive on seenit and also three borderline true positives (flag(), CLI-vs-MCP, and two near-identical stat components). Nothing counts what it wrongly discards.
The post-change labelled sample is n = 8, far too small. The 30-case pre-change sample remains the larger evidence base.
The p90 percentile is a judgement, chosen because it behaved on two repositories. It has not been set from an outcome the way the complexity thresholds were.
Both labelled repositories are JavaScript/TypeScript. Nothing is known about other languages.
Labelled by the tool's author. A floor-check, not an independent evaluation.

ranking.signal: longest aligned run — the largest set of shared fingerprints holding a constant (lineA - lineB) offset
ranking.why: Genuine copy-paste preserves a constant offset across the copied block; incidental matches between unrelated code scatter across many offsets. Raw overlap ranks by file size instead, which put a useState run (30 shared) above grade()-vs-healthColor() (13 shared).
ranking.separation: real duplication 10-27 aligned, idiomatic noise 3-8, no overlap on the labelled set
rejected: inverse document frequency — real 2.00 vs noise 2.70 mean files-per-shape, too close to rank on
contiguous line blocks — every case landed at 4-5, because winnowing samples lines too sparsely for blocks to differ
ranking.threshold: RELATIVE: this repository's own p90 of aligned runs, floored at 9. A fixed number cannot serve both ends — measured across 34 corpus repositories, the p99 of coincidental overlap has a median of 46 and reaches 349, while seenit's own p99 is 27 and vite's is 449. A flat 9 keeps a fifth of candidate pairs in a median repo; a flat 46 would delete every real find in a small one. Effect: vite 55 findings -> 4, seenit 5 -> 3. See results/alignment.json.

clustering: Pairs are grouped into findings by union-find over the clone graph: files transitively linked by clone pairs are one finding. seenit 8 pairs -> 5 findings; vite 468 -> 55.
